item.title: Football roundup: DeWitt adds to streak, Ithaca and P-W set up rematch
item.description: DEWITT 54, COOPERSVILLE 21 DEWITT — Griffin Braman ran for 129 yards and two touchdowns and threw for 63 yards and three touchdowns while helping the Panthers to a Division 3 district final win over Coopersville. Landon Kurncz added three catches for 47 yards and two touchdowns and Joseph Bobeda ran for 87 yards and a touchdown to help DeWitt win a third straight district title. The Panthers advance to face Mount Pleasant next week in a regional final in what is a rematch of last year's Division 3 state title game. PEWAMO-WESTPHALIA 41, ELKTON PIGEON-BAY PORT LAKER 7 WESTPHALIA — Caleb Blyth, Alex Nurenberg and Carter Thelen rushed for touchdowns and Alex Drysdale had a TD reception while contributing to the Pirates capturing a Division 7 district title with a win over Elkton-Pigeon-Bay Port Laker. Pewamo-Westphalia advances to face Ithaca in a regional final next week. ITHACA 39, MILLINGTON 16 MILLINGTON — Gibson Rondy completed 18-of-28 passes for 183 yards and a touchdown and ran for 144 yards and a score to help the Yellowjackets to a victory over Millington in a Division 7 district final. Devyn Fisher had six catches for 91 yards and a TD, the Yellowjackets returned a fumble for a score and Landon Bratschi made a 30-yard field for Ithaca (10-1). The Yellowjackets will face Pewamo-Westphalia next week in a regional final. GOODRICH 49, ST. JOHNS 7 GOODRICH — Conner Kurncz threw for 100 yards and Archer Gurski had a rushing score for the Redwings in their loss to Goodrich in a Division 4 district final. Goodrich jumped out to a 28-0 lead in the second quarter before Gurski scored the lone touchdown for St. Johns, which closes its season with an 8-3 record. item.description: BOSTON −The game didn’t matter nearly as much as the last time the two teams met, but the atmosphere was rocking for a November basketball game. Michigan basketball and UConn gave a capacity TD Garden crowd their money’s worth in a national championship game rematch seven months to the day. This time, however, the Huskies prevailed in an 85-77 victory, fueled by an 18-4 run covering the end of the first half and the first four minutes of the second half. U-M’s offense was stagnant much of the evening, shooting just 26-for-63 (41.3%) from the floor and 7-for-28 (25%) from 3. item.description: BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 06: Trey McKenney #1 of the Michigan Wolverines drives to the basket against Silas Demary Jr. #5 of the UConn Huskies during the first half at The TD Garden on November 06, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. item.title: Former Colts All-Pro OG Quenton Nelson to undergo cleanup surgery and will miss at least a few weeks
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 02: Quenton Nelson #53 of the Seattle Seahawks in action against the Chicago Bears at Lumen Field on November 02, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Former Indianapolis Colts All-Pro offensive guard Quenton Nelson, who was traded last week to the Seattle Seahawks for a 2027 3rd round pick and 2028 fifth round pick, will undergo minor cleanup cartilage surgery on his balky knee and miss at least a few weeks—although he’ll not be placed on injured reserve at this time: #Seahawks G Quenton Nelson will have surgery to clean out some cartilage in his knee, sources say, as fragments had been causing an issue recently. The plan is for Nelson to avoid Injured Reserve, and his timeline is a few weeks. Seattle has two games, then a Week 11 bye. pic.twitter.com/AZyUFzg7Kj — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 6, 2026 The Seahawks have two games and then their BYE week, so the hopeful expectation for Seattle must be that Nelson could be ready in 3 weeks’ time as opposed to the minimum 4-game period of inactivity that any stint on injured reserve requires before any ensuing activation. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald indicated that Nelson had the knee condition prior to arriving in Seattle via trade, having suffered it in on the road in Week 7 against the Minnesota Vikings while still formerly a member of the Colts. However, he aggravated the knee injury further, during the Seahawks’ 34-17 Monday Night home loss against the Chicago Bears. It’s unfortunate timing for the playoff hopeful Seahawks and Nelson, who was rather unsurprisingly very impressive during his Seahawks debut on primetime . The future Hall-of-Famer figured to be a ‘plug-and-play’ elite left guard for Seattle in no time and didn’t skip a beat during his Pacific Northwest debut. What is interesting is that it seems as though both the Colts and the Seahawks knew of Nelson’s initial knee condition, which likely came up in his physical. Although to be fair, it worsened this past Monday Night. Perhaps that may have been some of interim GM Ed Dodds’ eagerness and motivation in moving Nelson well before the trade deadline, knowing that his knee condition could eventually lead to the perennial All-Pro and pending NFL free agent missing games down the road in 2026. It’s hard to say for sure at this time. Nelson has been incredibly durable in his Canton-bound NFL career to-date, having only missed 4 starts—all of which occurred during the 2021 campaign with the Colts. We wish Big Q a speedy recovery the rest of the way.

item.title: Sean Wesolek cements his place in the Hope post, following 'older brothers'
item.description: HOLLAND - The Hope College men's basketball team has a good blend in the post. Orion Yant is long and lanky, Kyle Blauch is big and strong, then off the bench, Sean Wesolek is in between - and can shoot. Wesolek, a sophomore center, saw time last season, but will be relied upon for much more. He had the best game of his career in Hope's 90-63 season opening win over Anderson (Ind.) on Friday, Nov. 6, at DeVos Fieldhouse. Wesolek totaled 10 points and grabbed three rebounds in 13 key minutes off the bench. "He is a good combination of the two. It is huge because he gets rewarded for doing things the right way," Hope coach Greg Mitchell said. "All he wanted to do last year was learn. He hung out with Kyle and Orion and just soaked it all up. His attitude and charisma allow him to find his potential. He will be ready every game because he has so much respect for the guys before him, which is really cool." More: 'Two-headed monster' on point for Hope College women's basketball this season The 6-foot, 6-inch Bay City native scored four baskets in the paint and nailed a 3-pointer that keyed a run to put the Flying Dutch up double digits - something they didn't relinquish. "I definitely tried to get bigger this offseason. I gained 15 pounds. But I have two bigs in front of me that support me. When I do well, I feel more loved on than anybody," Wesolek said. "That is the difference between Hope and other places. We have guys who will love and support you no matter what." The post trio helped Hope grab 58 rebounds - 29 more than Anderson. Blauch had 13, including five on the offensive end. Yant had nine to go along with 14 points and two blocks. "It is so fun. We are like three brothers. I like to think of them as my older brothers. They took me in last year and it has been great," said Wesolek, whose older sister was an NCAA qualifier and captain for Hope swimming. "Our dynamic has been great. We each do different things well, and I think it is really unique to have that in a post." The guards played well for Hope, too, as Brandon Cargill totaled 20 points, four rebounds and two assists, while Avery Sanchez had 11 points, five rebounds and two assists. "We played really hard. It wasn't super clean. But we rebounded the heck our of it. Our biggest concern is if we are able to rebound. These guys listened," Mitchell said. "We are deep and we play hard. It is a really cohesive group … and we have to keep it rolling. We don't have any seniors but these guys have some big dreams and we have prove it every night." item.title: Windthorst QB Brock Belcher climbs to No. 3 on Texas all-time passing TD list
item.description: Windthorst senior quarterback Brock Belcher added another milestone to his record-setting career Friday, Nov. 6, moving into third place on Texas high school football's all-time passing touchdowns list across all classifications. Belcher threw three touchdown passes in the Trojans' 55-6 victory over Munday, bringing his career total to 168 and moving him past former Ennis quarterback Graham Harrell, who finished with 167. More: QB Cooper Corley's growth as leader fueling Graham football's playoff hopes More: No. 24 Midwestern State football looks to make a playoff push More: Photos of Windthorst vs. Munday high school football The senior entered the game with 38 touchdown passes this season and added scoring throws to three different receivers as Windthorst (9-1, 6-0) closed out the regular season with another dominant performance. Belcher completed 15 of 24 passes for 209 yards, three touchdowns and an interception. He also rushed six times for 49 yards and a touchdown, accounting for four scores in the victory. His first touchdown pass went to Ruben Willden for 30 yards in the opening quarter. Belcher later connected with Aiden Stark for a 15-yard score in the second quarter before finding Brodie Belz for a 21-yard touchdown in the third. The performance continued an impressive senior campaign for Belcher, who has now thrown 41 touchdown passes this season after recording 37 in 2024. Belcher trails only Refugio's Travis Quintanilla (186) and Sunray's Armando Lujan (171) on the UIL-era career passing touchdowns list maintained by Texas High School Football History. item.title: Crash Of The Titans: RV Marquette 93, Detroit Mercy 32
item.description: No one has published photos from the McGuire Center yet, so here’s Alex Egbuonu trying to end some poor guy from Mercyhurst. | Photo by Larry Radloff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images I don’t think there’s a lot of point in recapping Marquette’s 93-32 victory over Detroit Mercy on Friday night. It’s the second largest margin of victory in program history, trailing only a 67 point victory over Ripon on December 4, 1951. It’s the only 60+ margin of victory game against a team that’s currently in Division 1, and it’s just the second time that Marquette cleared 50+ as a margin since the 2001-02 season. Marquette set a KenPom era record for best defensive efficiency, surrendering just 0.475 points per possession. So, let’s just rattle off the runs that Marquette went on in this game. 6-0 10-0 to lead by 11 7-0 to lead by 15 9-0 to end the half up 22 Combine the last two for 16-2 over the final eight minutes of the first half. 7-0 to start the second half and lead by 29 Combine the last three for 23-2 5-0, and that’s 28-2 over a 14 minute stretch bridging halftime, Marquette by 32 15-0 to lead by 44 9-0 to lead by 51 Combine the last two for 24-2 in less than seven minutes 9-0 to lead by 58 Combine the last three for 33-4 in just under 10 minutes of game time And a nice little 5-0 over the final 1:42 to end the game. How about some stats! Leading scorer: Alex Egbuonu with 16 on 7-for-11 shooting Leading rebounder: Sananda Fru and Josh Clark both had 8 Assists leader: Nigel James had 8 in just 23 minutes Blocks leader: Josh Clark with 3 Steals leader: Nigel James with 4 Plus/minus leader: Josh Clark at +37 There’s so little to talk about here that they haven’t even uploaded the highlight reel yet. item.title: Gophers hold off late Tommie push, down St. Thomas 76-62
item.description: Isaac Asuma led all scorers with 20 points in a win over St. Thomas. University of St. Thomas leadership, alums and Patrick Reusse finally got their wish with a Minnesota/St. Thomas regular season contest, in an early-season tilt between the Twin Cities’s two Division I basketball programs. A matchup that hadn’t been revisited in almost 100 years, Minnesota finally relented and hosted the Tommies in what has surely been circled on UST’s calendar for months. And why not? The Tommie roster is chock full of metro kids who weren’t recruited by the Gophers and saw it as a chance to slay the state’s Goliath. It looked like it might be over early, with the Gophers racing out to a double-digit lead thanks to relentless defense and hot shooting from Isaac Asuma. Minnesota pushed that to a 20-point lead late in the half before going to the locker room with a 40-22 lead, holding the Tommies to just 23% shooting. The second half would be a different story, as St. Thomas clearly adjusted to make the Gophers work a little harder on defense, routinely finding seams and wide open looks on sloppy Minnesota rotations. Timely threes, a bevy of Gopher turnovers and easy missed shots opened the door for the Tommies to storm back into the game, cutting the lead to seven on multiple occasions. Minnesota bent but didn’t break, getting to the line effectively and doing just enough to stymie the St. Thomas comeback down the stretch, while walking away with a 76-62 victory and a 2-0 start to the season. It got a little hairy, but Minnesota’s size and strength advantage ultimately gave them a lot of room for error. THE STAT : Isaac Asuma led all scorers with 20 points. He hit four three-pointers in the first half, en route to 14 points. TURNING POINT : Minnesota went on a 16-0 run midway through the first half to push the lead to 17 at the time. This would provide enough cushion to largely coast through the second half and endure multiple St. Thomas runs. HOT : The Gophers were excellent from the free throw line and hit timely FTs when needed, going 19-22 from the line and halting Tommie momentum more than once. NOT : Bobby Durkin was largely MIA on offense and defense, going 1-6 from the field while scoring only five points. NOTABLE : With Kai Shinholster shelved for a month with a calf injury, Orono HS grad Nolan Groves served as the sixth man, playing 29 minutes off the bench and racking up 15 points. He looked good. DID YOU KNOW: Minnesota paid St. Thomas $100,000 for this game, though it is not expected to be a regular occurrence. Not surprising given that Minnesota gets nothing out of the deal other than the opportunity to potentially build the brand of a rival Division I program in its own backyard. UP NEXT : The Gophers hit the road and face Cincinnati on Monday for a true road game against a power conference opponent. It will be a good early-season barometer as the Bearcats, 2-0, are a similarly ranked KenPom team.

item.title: Celtics destroy struggling Hornets, 119-80, in wire-to-wire win
item.description: The Boston Celtics showed a struggling, shorthanded Charlotte Hornets squad no mercy on Friday night. The Green Team went up by as many as 46 points and ultimately prevailed 119-80 at the Spectrum Center, improving to 7-2 on the season and 2-0 in NBA Cup action. The blitz began almost immediately, as the Celtics jumped out to a 20-point lead in the first quarter and led by 31 points at halftime. The C's drained 17 triples in that first half, tying a franchise record, and ended up shooting 54.5 from deep in the lopsided win. Meanwhile, the Hornets shot 22 percent from beyond the arc and an astonishingly abysmal 29.3 percent from the floor. Simply put, the Celtics dominated every aspect of the game. They won the rebounding battle (51-43), doubled up the Hornets on blocks (8-4), and recorded a season-high 33 assists. And while the Hornets were without guard Kon Knueppel, point guard Dennis Schröder, center Moussa Diabaté, and forward Grant Williams due to injury, they never put up much of a fight — especially once forward Brandon Miller left the contest in the second quarter with groin soreness. Charlotte now finds itself on a six-game losing streak and at the bottom of the East Group C standings. Conversely, Boston is at the top of the East Group C standings with a massive point differential and has a great shot at advancing past the group stage of the NBA Cup. item.title: Tim Tebow Issues Tough Reality Check for Pete Golding’s Ole Miss Before They Face Kirby Smart’s Georgia: “It’s Too Difficult”
item.description: ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire Georgia’s defense is suffocating opponents, and college football legend Tim Tebow says Ole Miss faces one nearly insurmountable problem. If they suffer a loss, that will drop the Rebels’ playoff odds to a bleak 41%, and their single path to victory depends on a running game that is now severely compromised. Tim Tebow joined Matt Barrie on Friday to break down exactly what Pete Golding needs to do to survive this matchup. Georgia enters with one loss, while Ole Miss sits with two losses, meaning a win keeps Georgia’s national championship hopes alive, while a loss for Ole Miss likely ends their playoff chances. “I think this Georgia defense is too good. They’re not the same Georgia defense that Ole Miss played last year,” Tebow warned , dropping a serious reality check on Pete Golding’s squad. “With Chris Cole, Raylen Wilson, I think they’re going to be spying on him. Second and third and long, I think it’s too difficult. So you got to be able to get a good enough running game to keep this Georgia defense balanced.” Well, you only have to look at how downright terrifying Kirby Smart’s defense has been throughout the year! The Dawgs have been suffocating opponents with their run defense, giving up a microscopic 86.0 rushing yards per game on a mere 2.7 yards per carry. Tebow's blunt assessment reveals what Ole Miss must overcome to compete with Georgia's elite defense. Stay tuned for expert breakdown of this crucial SEC matchup. And it’s not just the run game. The secondary is making life miserable for quarterbacks through the air, while the defense is allowing only 14.9 points per game to rank among the elite in the country. Last season, Ole Miss’s Trinidad Chambliss led the Rebels to a win over Georgia with a clutch performance, but repeating that feat won’t come easy against this year’s Bulldogs. item.title: Michigan handed first loss in national title game rematch against UConn
item.description: BOSTON — It seemed like the Wolverines were walking into a lion’s den. A motivated UConn team that was out for revenge. A rowdy crowd that was buzzing from start to finish. An essential true road game at a neutral site. In a rematch of last season’s national championship game, No. 20 Michigan couldn’t overcome a rough finish to the first half and a lackluster shooting performance in an 85-77 loss to No. 5 UConn on Friday, Nov. 6 at TD Garden. Trey McKenney scored 22 – all coming in the second half – J.P. Estrella had 19 points and nine rebounds, and Roddy Gayle Jr. added 18 points for Michigan (1-1), which shot 41.3% from the field (26-for-63) and trailed much of the way. The Wolverines, despite struggling to make shots outside the paint, stayed in contact throughout much of the first half until the Huskies closed that half on a 9-0 run to build a 13-point lead. And on a night where Michigan’s offense could never get comfortable and shot 7-for-28 from 3-point range, that hole continued to grow in the second half. Two 3-pointers from Jayden Ross widened UConn’s margin to 52-34 with 16:22 to play. The Wolverines chipped away at deficit behind McKenney. After a scoreless first half where he missed all seven of his shots, McKenney came alive and scored 11 points in the span of 4:11 to cut it to single digits. Most of his damage came from deep, where he hit three 3-pointers in less than three minutes to pull Michigan within 64-55 with 9:25 to play. Not enough stops and too many fouls prevented Michigan from climbing all the way back, as UConn pushed the lead back to double digits in a flash. A live-ball turnover by the Wolverines preceded a putback by the Huskies. A missed 3-pointer by Michigan was followed by a deep ball by UConn. Just like that, Michigan trailed 69-55 at the 8:11 mark. The Wolverines could never get closer than eight the rest of the way as they couldn’t pass their first real test of the regular season. item.title: Villanova secures needed bounce back win vs. Holy Cross in home opener
item.description: ROME, ITALY - NOVEMBER 01: Luigi Suigo of Villanova Wildcats reacts during the Eternal City Tip-Off Men's Game between Villanova and Notre Dame at Palazzo dello Sport on November 01, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was not the biggest early-season challenge for Villanova, but it was the game that the team needed following a season-opening loss to Notre Dame. Villanova had five players finish in double figures and shot 51% from the field, knocking down 10 three’s, during a 95-66 win over Holy Cross in the first game of the season at the Finneran Pavilion. The Wildcats came into the game needing to show some improvements from the first game of the year. It began immediately as Villanova opened up its first double-digit lead eight minutes into the game. From there, the offense was able to keep extending into the second half when the lead eventually ballooned above 30. The starting frontcourt of Devin Royal and Luigi Suigo stepped up in the absence of Kwame Evans Jr., who missed the game with a leg injury he has been dealing with since the preseason. Suigo stayed out of foul trouble and showed off his full skillset down low, logging a double-double with 16 points and 15 rebounds on 8-for-9 from the field. Royal led the Wildcats with 22 points on 9-for-16 shooting. Villanova got the chance to show off its depth as well. Adam Oumiddoch scored 17 points in 22 minutes off the bench. Aside from Tyler Perkins, who shot just 2-for-12, the Wildcats impressed on the offensive end. Perhaps the most impressive was Jake Fiegen, who proved that he can provide a spark from three-point range, finishing with 15 points on 5-for-6 from deep. Villanova will be back in action on Tuesday against La Salle.

item.title: Colts rookie LB CJ Allen will be handling important defensive duty on Sunday for first time
item.description: JACKSONVILLE, FL - NOVEMBER 01: CJ Allen #53 of the Indianapolis Colts reacts after a play during the game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Indianapolis Colts on November 1, 2026 at EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Fl. (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Indianapolis Colts rookie starting linebacker CJ Allen, who was originally a top candidate to don the infamous green dot during training camp, will assume such duties for the first time in his NFL career on Sunday at home against the Dallas Cowboys. As starting veteran linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee) was already ruled out, the green dot duties at the 2nd level of the Indy defense will now transition to Allen, who at MIKE, will be making his 2nd career NFL start. With Davis-Gaither unlikely to be re-signed as a veteran free agent at year-end, it’s quite possible that the Colts will let Allen don the defense’s lone built-in radio speaker and handle communicating the defensive play-calling to his on-the-field Indianapolis teammates the rest of the way. There’d be no real reason not to, unless it goes poorly. Allen was one of the few silver linings during last Sunday’s blowout road loss the Jacksonville Jaguars, recording a team-high 10 tackles to go along with a sack. He projects to be a potential key piece to the Colts defensive core if he can continue to improve and develop after such an encouraging debut start last weekend. That being said, he’ll be handling an important job duty, and one that was already the center of an unnecessarily self-inflicted controversy to start the Colts’ disappointing 2026 season—as veteran safety Cam Bynum initially handled green dot duties in the Colts Week 1 loss to the Baltimore Ravens. There was a number of breakdowns and Colts defensive players being out of position, as Bynum was forced to run from down the field and the backend of the Indy secondary to relay the defensive play-calling to his teammates, which didn’t provide them as much opportunity to communicate and get set pre-snap. At that time, the Colts were the only team not to use a linebacker for handling green dot duties, and it cost them in Week 1. Here’s hoping Allen’s green dot debut goes a lot smoother!
